2608.08173.title: $\texttt{DisMorph}$: learning to disentangle technical distortions from true biological change
2608.08173.paper_summary: Longitudinal MRI enables sensitive measurement of structural brain change for studying aging and neurodegenerative disease. Deformable image registration is a key tool for estimating such change by computing a dense deformation that captures geometric differences between longitudinal scans. However, MRI scanners introduce geometric distortions that vary across acquisition systems and protocols, such as gradient non-linearity (GNL) distortion. Existing registration methods estimate a single field that conflates biological and technical effects, potentially biasing downstream morphometric measurements if distortions remain (partially) uncorrected. We propose $\texttt{DisMorph}$, a registration framework trained entirely on synthetic data that explicitly decomposes longitudinal deformation into technical and anatomical transforms. It predicts two dense deformations, each encoding one effect. During training, a novel generative model synthesizes both effects separately to provide disentanglement supervision, while domain randomization promotes generalization across imaging protocols. We evaluate our method in three complementary settings. On simulated data with known ground truth, our method detects anatomical change more accurately and consistently than conventional registration. On real image pairs that differ only by GNL distortion, our method assigns most geometric change to the distortion field, demonstrating specificity in the absence of anatomical change. On longitudinal Alzheimer's disease (AD) pairs, our method detects anatomical change in AD-related brain structures while identifying residual distortion left after standard correction. By disentangling MRI-induced distortion from biological change in the longitudinal deformation, our method paves the way for more accurate longitudinal morphometry in clinical settings where maintaining acquisition consistency is challenging.
2608.08173.paper_summary_zh: 長期的MRI能夠敏感地測量結構性腦部變化，以研究老化和神經退行性疾病。可變形影像配準是估計此類變化的關鍵工具，通過計算捕捉長期掃描之間幾何差異的密集變形來實現。然而，MRI掃描儀引入的幾何失真在不同的獲取系統和協議中有所不同，例如梯度非線性（GNL）失真。現有的配準方法估計一個單一的場，將生物學和技術效果混合在一起，如果失真（部分）未被修正，則可能會對下游的形態測量產生偏差。我們提出了$\texttt{DisMorph}$，這是一個完全基於合成數據訓練的配準框架，明確地將長期變形分解為技術和解剖變換。它預測兩個密集的變形，每個變形編碼一種效果。在訓練過程中，一種新穎的生成模型分別合成這兩種效果，以提供解耦監督，而領域隨機化促進了跨影像協議的泛化。我們在三個互補的設置中評估我們的方法。在具有已知真實值的模擬數據上，我們的方法比傳統配準更準確且一致地檢測到解剖變化。在僅因GNL失真而不同的真實影像對上，我們的方法將大多數幾何變化分配給失真場，顯示出在缺乏解剖變化的情況下的特異性。在長期阿茲海默病（AD）影像對上，我們的方法檢測到與AD相關的腦結構中的解剖變化，同時識別在標準修正後留下的殘餘失真。通過將MRI引起的失真與長期變形中的生物變化解耦，我們的方法為在維持獲取一致性挑戰的臨床環境中進行更準確的長期形態測量鋪平了道路。
